package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package, but rather discusses the macro-level risks and attack vectors in the software supply chain that can lead to malicious compromise, such as credential theft, tampering with build environments, and injection of malware into open-source components.

execution_context.file_location: build environment (e.g., build scripts, CI/CD pipeline)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Adversary infiltrates build environment and introduces malicious changes to digitally signed code.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (could be shell, python, or language of the build system)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, the code modifies the build artifacts to include malicious payloads, which are then digitally signed and distributed to downstream customers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying build artifacts to include unauthorized code is a classic supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build environments are expected to produce trusted, verified code; unauthorized changes violate this trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build scripts legitimately modify and package code, but only as intended by the development team.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious actor accesses and exfiltrates API security tokens and secrets from CI/CD pipeline environment variables.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (could be shell, python, or language of the CI/CD scripts)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the CI/CD pipeline, the code reads sensitive environment variables (API tokens, secrets) and sends them to an external server, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating secrets from CI/CD environments is a high-impact attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CI/CD pipelines are expected to keep secrets confidential and not transmit them externally.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may use secrets to deploy or test, but should never exfiltrate them.
key_indicators: Network requests to unknown domains during CI/CD runs
Secrets found in logs or external transmissions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware injected into open-source component or third-party library, executed when imported or installed.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or installation, the code executes malicious payloads, which may exfiltrate data, open backdoors, or tamper with the host system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected code execution during import or install is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Dependencies are expected to provide only their documented functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages run setup scripts for legitimate reasons, but should not perform network exfiltration or system tampering.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or undocumented code in dependencies
Access to sensitive files or environment variables

attack_chain.action: Adversary gains access to build environment or CI/CD pipeline.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify build artifacts or access secrets.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code or configuration is injected into build artifacts or open-source dependencies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payloads are distributed to downstream users.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in customer environments, exfiltrating data or enabling further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, data exfiltration, or system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during build, install, or import stages
Access to sensitive environment variables in CI/CD pipelines
Modification of build artifacts not reflected in source code
Obfuscated or undocumented code in dependencies
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in build scripts or pipeline configs
Presence of unknown or suspicious files in build artifacts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during build or CI/CD runs
Exfiltration of secrets to external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build and CI/CD environments for unauthorized changes to artifacts, unexpected network activity, and access to sensitive environment variables. Use binary analysis to compare released artifacts with source code. Scan dependencies for obfuscated or undocumented code and monitor for unexpected file or network behaviors during installation or import.
